summary: The integration endpoints. `/integration/health` reports connectivity, versions, AI mode, live clients and a self-describing endpoint catalog, `/integration/metrics` serves the request and latency figures collected by `iip/observability.py`, and `/stream` is the Server-Sent Events endpoint that streams `LiveHub` messages from `iip/live.py` to every open dashboard (`web/js/core/live.js`).

`endpoint_catalog` builds the list of every API endpoint shown on the Integration page.
The catalog is read from the generated OpenAPI schema, the same document behind `/docs`, so it can never drift from the real routes: add an endpoint and it appears automatically.

`app.openapi()` returns the schema as a dict (FastAPI builds it once and caches it); its `paths` section maps each URL to its operations.
Each operation is keyed by its HTTP method (`get`, `post`, `patch`).
An endpoint counts as secured if it declares an `x-api-key` header parameter, which is how the `require_api_key` dependency shows up in the schema.

Returns the metrics snapshot (request counts, error rate, latency percentiles, per-route stats, throughput) with the live client count added.
Registers `GET /api/v1/stream`, the endpoint browsers connect to with `EventSource`.
Declared `async` because it does no blocking work; the async generator it returns is consumed on the event loop, the same loop `call_soon_threadsafe` delivers messages to.

Wraps this client's `hub.stream()` generator in a `StreamingResponse`. `text/event-stream` is the content type `EventSource` requires, `Cache-Control: no-cache` stops anything caching the stream, and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` tells an nginx proxy not to buffer it, so each event reaches the browser immediately.
